chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And whoever inclines therein to wrong unjustly, We will make him taste of a painful punishment.' He said: 'Every injustice that a man commits against himself in Mecca, from theft, or being unjust to anyone, or any of the injustices, then I consider it to be heresy (ilhad), and due to that, one should fear from residing in the Sanctuary (al-Haram).'

key_terms.إِلْحَاد: Heresy or inclining to wrong; here interpreted as committing injustice.
key_terms.الْحَرَمُ: The Sanctuary (referring to Mecca and its sacred boundaries).
key_terms.يَتَّقَى: To fear or be cautious of.

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq define as 'ilhad' (heresy) in Mecca according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expands the concept of 'ilhad' beyond mere heresy to encompass any form of injustice or oppression committed within the sanctity of Mecca, including theft and personal wrongs. This broad interpretation underscores the heightened spiritual accountability in the holy city, leading to the scholarly recommendation of avoiding permanent residence there to minimize the risk of incurring such grave sins.
